result.title: Parametric Modelling for Personalized Prosthetics
result.summary: No study in this literature directly compared script-based and graphical parametric modeling for upper limb prosthetics, but the repeated convergence of graphical-tool users toward externalized, script-like automation strategies—alongside persistent gaps in embedded DfAM constraints and clinical accessibility—strongly suggests that script-based tools offer untapped advantages in reproducibility, conditional geometry logic, and manufacturing rule integration, with their principal limitation being a usability barrier for non-engineering clinical users.
